# LSP study: does LSP help Claude Code?

> A controlled comparison of Claude Code agents with and without language-server (LSP) tools: 2,232 runs on 87 tasks in 29 projects, three Claude models (Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5), 9 programming languages. Across 87 tasks, offering the LS (optional arm) changed success by +0.3 points (interval -2.1 to +3.0) at 1.02× the baseline cost. Pushing the agent to use it (enforced arm) changed success by -2.0 points (interval -5.2 to +1.0) at 1.57× the cost. A second review turn without any LS (baseline-review) cost 2.34×.

What is tested: tereditor (https://github.com/CommanderTvis/tereditor), an IDE-like workbench for terminal coding agents whose headless build serves a project's language server to an agent over MCP. Its six tools: lsp_navigate (definitions, references, implementations, symbols, call hierarchies, one read-only LSP query), lsp_diagnostics (errors for edited files or the workspace), lsp_rename, lsp_code_actions and lsp_format (preview before writing, workspace only), lsp_status (servers and capabilities). Example call: lsp_navigate {"operation": "references", "query": "PaymentCardNumber", "workspace": "/workspace"} returns the reference locations with zero-based lines and previews.

Arms: baseline (Claude Code core tools only: Read, Edit, Write, Bash, Task, ToolSearch); baseline-review (baseline plus a second review turn); optional (LSP tools offered, not required); enforced (LSP use pushed by prompt and hooks); intellij-optional and intellij-enforced (IntelliJ as the language server, JVM projects only; on Kotlin the plain optional and enforced arms use https://github.com/Kotlin/kotlin-lsp). Success is a deterministic grader's pass rate; cost is Claude Code's total_cost_usd. Contrasts are paired on tasks; intervals are 95% task-resampling intervals.

## Findings

- Success: offering LS tools (optional) and enforcing them (enforced) do not change the pass rate by a clear amount. Both intervals include zero.
- Flaws: paired on the same tasks, optional LS tools change flaws by -0.14 flaws per run (95% interval -0.40 to +0.04), no clear difference. Enforced LS use leaves more: +0.26 flaws per run (95% interval +0.07 to +0.47).
- Cost: optional costs about the same as baseline; enforced costs about 1.57 times as much.
- Adoption: when offered, the agent uses LS tools in 16% of optional runs on Opus and in none on Haiku or Sonnet.
- Task kinds: 58 synthetic tasks (9 types) and 29 real pull-request tasks. Both are reported separately on the page.
- Java and Kotlin: the sample is small (12 pure Java tasks, 12 Kotlin and mixed tasks); every interval includes zero.

## Data

- [runs.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/runs.csv): one row per run (task, arm, model, tool calls, cost, turns, success)
- [plan.tsv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/plan.tsv): the seeded run plan
- [flaws.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/flaws.csv): every quality flaw the reviewer reported (run, kind, file, line, reason)
- [descriptive.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/descriptive.csv): success, cost, time and LSP use per model and arm
- [contrasts.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/contrasts.csv): paired contrasts against the baseline, all tasks
- [by_model.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/by_model.csv), [by_lang.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/by_lang.csv), [by_size.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/by_size.csv), [by_task_type.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/by_task_type.csv), [by_probe_half.csv](https://commandertvis.github.io/tereditor-lsp-research/data/by_probe_half.csv): the same contrasts by stratum
